questions.question: Rematerialization reduces the number of saved residual descriptions but the compiled temporary-byte estimates are equal. What is the supported conclusion?
options: The compiler’s report must be wrong.
The differentiation strategy changed, but this evidence does not show reduced compiled temporary storage.
The model must train faster because fewer values were listed.
questions.explanation: Residual lists and compiler buffer estimates describe different levels. Report the observed equality and investigate the real target workload before claiming a memory or speed benefit.
optionFeedback: AD residuals and compiler temporary-buffer estimates describe different stages. Fewer saved intermediates need not lower the reported buffer peak.
Residual lists and compiler buffer estimates describe different levels. Report the observed equality and investigate the real target workload before claiming a memory or speed benefit.
Rematerialization trades storage for recomputation. Measure latency and peak memory separately before claiming an improvement.
